t: The Strange Case of Dr Jekyll and Mr Hyde

paper-1-shakespeare-and-post-1914-litera: 'This is a metaphor' earns almost nothing. What makes it analysis?
paper-2-19th-century-novel-and-poetry-si: One printed scene, a question on the whole play. Where do you start?
romeo-and-juliet: The Prologue gives away the ending. Why would Shakespeare do that?
a-christmas-carol: Why does Scrooge's whole life change in a single night?
an-inspector-calls: Why end the play with a phone call, not an arrest?
poetry-anthology-collection: Hidden anger grows into a tree. Who ends up poisoned?
relationships-poetry: She said 'I love thee true'. So why is the knight left dying?
time-and-place-poetry: Autumn means things ending. Why does Keats make it feel so full?
belonging-poetry: He tells his sister to leave her book. Is Wordsworth anti-learning?
unseen-poetry: A poem you've never seen, twenty minutes. What do you look for first?
macbeth: A brave hero in Act 1, a 'dead butcher' by Act 5. What went wrong?
the-merchant-of-venice: Three weddings and a happy ending. So why do many audiences not laugh?
much-ado-about-nothing: Two love stories, one play. Why does Shakespeare need both?
the-tempest: Twelve years of wrongs, settled in one afternoon. How?
twelfth-night: A love story and a prank on a steward. Why put both in one play?
the-strange-case-of-dr-jekyll-and-mr-hyd: Why does the novel hide its biggest secret until the last chapter?
great-expectations: Why does Dickens split Pip's life into three "stages"?
jane-eyre: Five homes, one girl. Why does Jane's story keep moving her on?
frankenstein: Why does a novel about a monster open with letters from a ship?
pride-and-prejudice: The novel's first line states a 'truth'. Should you believe it?
silas-marner: Why does the novel jump sixteen years in the middle?
